# Orlando — priors registered before menu capture

**Written 2026-08-23. No Orlando menu has been captured. Do not edit after capture — a wrong
prior is informative and quietly correcting it destroys the only evidence that the method was
tested rather than fitted.**

| # | prediction | falsified if |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Chain nutrition sheets will yield more usable dish-level phe estimates than the entire Asheville corpus | fewer usable estimates than Asheville's 299-dish census produced |
| 2 | Michelin-tier Orlando restaurants will show *worse* menu-fit counts than Asheville's, because the selection skews to protein-centred fine dining and sushi | Orlando's no-protein-source-named rate meets or beats Asheville's 63/299 |
| 3 | Counter-service density will make Orlando score highest of the three cities on camouflage | Copenhagen or Asheville scores higher |
| 4 | Disney's published policy will be the only Tier-2 operator policy in Orlando that names low-protein or PKU explicitly | a second operator names it |
| 5 | Starch anchors will skew harder to potato than Asheville's 30/109, because of fry-heavy quick service | potato share of named starch is at or below Asheville's 27.5% |

## Note on prediction 2

It is worth being clear that this prior expects the Michelin layer to look *bad* here. If it does,
that is not a problem with Orlando — it is evidence for the position that award recognition has no
relationship to whether a family can eat, which is the argument the whole registry design rests
on. Recording it in advance so the result cannot be presented as a surprise either way.
